title: The Town Mouse and the Country Mouse
source: Aesop's Fables (public domain), gently retold for bedtime

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Once upon a time, in a quiet meadow at the edge of a wheat field, there lived a little country mouse.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Her home was a cosy burrow under the roots of an old hedge, with a soft bed of moss, and a window that looked out at the stars.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: One sunny morning, a visitor came hurrying down the lane. It was her cousin, the town mouse, in his smart little coat.

lines.speaker: town
lines.speech: [cheerful, a little grand] Hello, dear cousin! I've come all the way from the big town, just to see you!
lines.text: Hello, dear cousin! I've come all the way from the big town, just to see you!

lines.speaker: country
lines.speech: [delighted, warm] Cousin! What a lovely surprise! Come in, come in. You must be hungry after your long walk.
lines.text: Cousin! What a lovely surprise! Come in, come in. You must be hungry after your long walk.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The country mouse set out the very best food she had. Some barley seeds, a few blackberries, and a little piece of crunchy corn.

lines.speaker: town
lines.speech: [politely, but unimpressed] Oh... seeds and berries. How... simple.
lines.text: Oh... seeds and berries. How... simple.

lines.speaker: town
lines.speech: [eager, persuasive] Cousin, you must come and visit me in town! I eat cakes, and cheese, and jelly every day. You've never tasted anything so wonderful!
lines.text: Cousin, you must come and visit me in town! I eat cakes, and cheese, and jelly every day. You've never tasted anything so wonderful!

lines.speaker: country
lines.speech: [curious, excited] Cakes and jelly? Oh, my! Alright, cousin. I'll come!
lines.text: Cakes and jelly? Oh, my! Alright, cousin. I'll come!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: So the two mice set off together. Over the hill, along the lane, and all the way into the big, busy town.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The town mouse lived in a grand old house, with tall windows, and soft carpets, and a great big dining room.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: On the long table, there was a feast. Cream cakes, and cheeses, and wobbly red jelly.

lines.speaker: town
lines.speech: [proud, sweeping] There you are, cousin. Help yourself!
lines.text: There you are, cousin. Help yourself!

lines.speaker: country
lines.speech: [amazed, softly] Oh... I've never seen so much food in all my life!
lines.text: Oh... I've never seen so much food in all my life!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: But just as she took her very first nibble of cake... the door creaked open.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: In padded the house cat. Big, and fluffy, and yawning. Meow!

lines.speaker: town
lines.speech: [urgent whisper] Quick, cousin! Run! Into the mouse hole!
lines.text: Quick, cousin! Run! Into the mouse hole!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Scurry, scurry, scurry! The two mice ran across the table, down the tablecloth, and into a tiny hole in the wall.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: They waited, and waited, in the dark. Their little hearts were going thump, thump, thump. At last, the sleepy cat wandered away.

lines.speaker: country
lines.speech: [gently, thoughtful] Cousin... thank you for showing me your fine house. But I think I'd like to go home now.
lines.text: Cousin... thank you for showing me your fine house. But I think I'd like to go home now.

lines.speaker: country
lines.speech: [warmly, sure] I would rather eat my seeds and berries in peace, than cakes and jelly with a cat at the door.
lines.text: I would rather eat my seeds and berries in peace, than cakes and jelly with a cat at the door.

lines.speaker: town
lines.speech: [softly, understanding, a small chuckle] I understand, cousin. Every mouse has her own kind of home.
lines.text: I understand, cousin. Every mouse has her own kind of home.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: So the country mouse walked all the way back to her quiet field. The sun was setting, and the wheat was gold.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She crept into her cosy burrow, ate a few sweet blackberries, and snuggled into her soft bed of moss.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Because a simple home, full of peace and quiet, is the best home of all.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Outside her little window, the stars came out, one by one. And far away in the big town, her cousin was fast asleep too.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Goodnight, little one. Sweet dreams.
